candidates.caption:
Face au changement climatique, des millions de petits agriculteurs doivent trouver des solutions pour protéger leurs récoltes et leurs moyens de subsistance.

C’est pour les aider que Rikin Gandhi a créé FarmerChat, un outil qui accompagne déjà plus de 2 millions d’agriculteurs.

J’ai eu la chance de le rencontrer à Goalkeepers, un événement organisé par la @gatesfoundation pendant la Climate Week, qui met en lumière celles et ceux qui font avancer le monde.

👉 Abonne-toi pour découvrir d’autres initiatives qui changent des vies !

Invitation voyage de presse

media.transcript: Cet Indien vient de changer la vie de millions d'agriculteurs grâce à une application révolutionnaire. Tout commence lorsque Rikin Gandhi, qui travaillait comme chercheur chez Microsoft, remarque un problème. Chaque fois qu'il montre aux agriculteurs des vidéos pour leur apprendre de nouvelles techniques à l'école, ils ont énormément de questions. Le problème, c'est qu'une vidéo ne peut pas leur répondre. Alors, avec l'essor de l'intelligence artificielle, il a une idée brillante. Farmer Chat. Les agriculteurs n'ont qu'à sortir leur téléphone, prendre une photo ou envoyer un message vocal dans leur langue maternelle s'ils ne sont pas à l'aise à l'écrit. L'IA peut alors les aider à identifier une maladie qui touche leur culture, à choisir le bon moment pour planter ou à répondre à tous les autres problèmes qu'ils peuvent rencontrer sur leur exploitation. Et si je vous en parle aujourd'hui, c'est parce que j'ai eu la chance de rencontrer Rick Keane à Goalkeepers, un événement organisé par la Fondation Gates. La fondation finance des recherches et des projets pour lutter contre la pauvreté, les maladies et les inégalités dans le monde. A travers Goalkeepers, elle réunit des scientifiques, des dirigeants et des acteurs de terrain comme Rick Keane qui ont trouvé des solutions témoignant de progrès concrets. Et cet événement se déroule pendant l'Assemblée Générale des Nations Unies et la Climate Week, donc toute une semaine, qui rassemble des dirigeants, des entreprises et des organisations autour de plus de 1000 événements pour accélérer l'action contre le changement climatique.

candidates.caption: 🌹 Si tu ROSAL tiene MANCHAS NEGRAS, puntas secas y hojas amarillas, no cortes las hojas sin antes hacer esto: este sencillo TRUCO puede ayudarte a controlar el problema antes de que siga avanzando.  #TrucosDeJardinería #CuidadoDePlantas #JardínFeliz

media.transcript: Si tu rosal, osmantus o cualquier otra planta empieza a sacar manchas negras, puntas secas o zonas amarillas, no cortes las hojas y te olvides del problema, porque si la causa sigue ahí, las manchas pueden volver a aparecer. Muchas veces, estas señales están relacionadas con problemas de hongos, especialmente cuando hay demasiada humedad y poca ventilación. Para ayudar a controlar el problema, puedes preparar una mezcla sencilla con tres dientes de ajo triturados, un litro de agua, una cucharada de alcohol y unas gotas de jabón. Mézclalo bien y colócalo en un atomizador. Después pulveriza las hojas afectadas, incluyendo la parte de abajo, porque ahí también pueden quedar problemas que no vemos. Hazlo de manera constante y observa cómo responde la planta. Y recuerda, si las manchas siguen avanzando, no basta con tratar las hojas. También hay que revisar el riego, la ventilación y las condiciones de la planta. Guarda este consejo para cuando aparezcan las primeras manchas.

candidates.caption: I Turned 1 Dragonfruit Into 100 Cactuses🐉 Normally you’d throw moldy dragonfruit in the garbage, but I placed it in a terracotta pot to see if I could grow 100+ baby dragons. Since dragonfruits grow into cactuses…I was hyped to see if they would really grow.🐉 Well guess what? It did grow and now I have an army of baby cactuses in my house! This….is the full story!👀 I was able to track every stage of my experiment using my app: Grow It! There are over 400 experiments to try out…so download it and start one with me!!  The links to download on the App Store and Google Play are below!   🔗Download ‘GROW IT!’ On the APP STORE Here:  https://apps.apple.com/ca/app/grow-it-plant-scanner-lab/id6762371470 🔗Download ‘GROW IT!’ On the GOOGLE PLAY Here: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.growithjessie.growit&pcampaignid=web_share

media.transcript: I wanted to see how many cactuses I could grow from one moldy dragon fruit. And when I realized this was in my fridge, I had two choices. Throw this old moldy dragon fruit in the garbage, or place it in a terracotta pot and try to turn it into a hundred baby dragons. And that's basically when my experiment began. First, I cut it in half. You can see the middle was starting to get pretty mushy. So I peeled away the skin until I was left with just the fruit. Then I had to figure out how exactly I was going to separate the tiny seeds from the actual fruit. So I got a strainer, rinsed the fruit underwater while rubbing it through the strainer until most of the fruit fell through the tiny holes and I was left with a lot of seeds. And that's when I realized that it might actually be possible to grow way more than just 100 cactuses here. because there were way more seeds in this thing than I was initially expecting. So I grabbed a little pot and started placing the seeds right on top. The only problem was that there was still a good amount of fruit stuck to the seeds, but I figured it would break down and disintegrate in the soil anyway. Once I had a nice layer of dragon fruit right on top, I covered it up and placed that outside in a sunny spot. But I noticed there were still at least a hundred seeds still sitting in that strainer. And my thought was, why would I throw them away if my end goal was to turn one moldy dragon fruit into a mini desert in my backyard? So I figured I'll give us options just in case something happens with the ones in the pot. I collected as many seeds as I could from that strainer and spread them out on a damp piece of paper towel. That initial strainer idea to separate the seeds to me was absolutely genius. I was tracking every step of this experiment in the Grow It app, so after I scanned my dragon fruit, I got the idea from there. Otherwise, I probably would have just cut the fruit and put it right in soil or dab the fruit on the paper towel to remove some of the seeds that way. But I folded that up, placed it in a little bag airtight, labeled it. I was really curious to see which one was going to grow faster. So I waited for one week. Well in just seven days I saw the first few dragons in soil start to sprout. As for the paper towel, I was pretty surprised because I was not expecting those seeds to already be poking out of that paper towel in just a week. So I opened it up and I was so pleased to see that these were actually growing a lot faster than the ones in soil. I decided to leave those in the paper towel and one week later I went to check on the soil first to see that even more little green sprouts were poking out. Then I went to check on the paper towel and saw the sprouts on that towel looking awesome. I actually couldn't believe how quickly they were growing. So I got a big pot and decided to just throw the paper towel straight into the big pot where my cucamelons were also growing. I figured the moisture would hold better in the paper towel and help the little sprouts actually start to turn into cactuses. But this was the hard part where I had to wait a few months and the progress over those few months was insane. No wonder why dragon fruits have one of the highest germination rates of any fruit. And by the way, you can download the Grow It app on the App Store and on Google Play. There's a library of 400 plus experiments that you can try out. I've linked it in the description below and in my bio. Well week after week I continued to check on our dragons. This was week three. Finally you could see the sprouts getting taller But they still looked more like regular little seedlings than cactuses. By week four more and more were shooting up And now the soil was almost fully covered with an entire carpet just as I suspected. Oddly from week four to week five there was not much visible growth that took place but it wasn't until I looked really closely that I could see some of the sprouts starting to form tiny little spikes. They were finally starting to turn into actual sharp cactuses but they were still really tiny and apparently one of our dragons escaped because I found this growing in a completely different pot. It must have been windy outside because I definitely didn't plant that there. As for the ones from the paper towel that we planted in that big pot, they were growing too. Slowly though, but you could see the little sharp tips of the cactuses also starting to form and I just got my first cucamelon today, so everything in this pot is doing quite well, but it's safe to say I was just excited for the weeks to continue passing. By week seven, our cactuses were finally starting to actually look like bigger cactuses. Those tiny little sprouts were getting thicker and you could see more spiky parts forming all the way up the middle. It was a very exciting day for me but I had to continue waiting. By week 8, just two months after starting this experiment, I finally realized something. There had to be at least 100 cactuses, if not even closer to 500 in this pot and they were getting pretty overcrowded but I was excited because as I tracked the experiment in the Grow It app, this is exactly what was supposed to happen. The seedlings began developing their distinctive succulent ribbed cactus form and growing them in small clusters at this point was also apparently fine. But a hundred cactuses obviously weren't going to fit in this little pot forever. If they were fine growing in small clusters, then I was okay with waiting to transplant them to avoid killing them altogether because they were all looking so healthy. Part of me wanted to see just how big they could actually get before I moved them. So I let them grow in peace until week 10 came around. And our baby dragons were not looking so baby anymore. And those spiky edges were becoming way more noticeable and defined straight down the middle. At this point they were finally starting to look like the dragon fruit cactuses I was hoping for and the image I had in my head. Basically just miniature versions of the giant dragon fruit cactuses they eventually become. So I kept giving them lots of sun, water and most importantly time. And another week of waiting led me to this. And every time I check on them they look more and more like actual cactuses. It's crazy to think that just a few months ago every single one of these was just a tiny black seed inside what I almost threw in the garbage. Hopefully they'll get just as big as this. This one I found on the side of the road one year ago and I've been growing them ever since. So they're obviously able to grow indoors in the winter just fine. Which means I think it's finally time to separate our baby dragons, bring them inside under the grow lights for the winter and see just how good they're going to grow. big we can actually get these to grow. For now the only thing on my mind is thinking about what to do with the other moldy dragon fruit that I've got in my fridge.

We wanted it to navigate the office and ID other plants. And Nano Banana, to sketch what the casing would look like. Whether it was on the design or the fabrication process, it was really nice to have like this amazing co-pilot. The base is a turtle bot, basically a Roomba with a chassis, a camera and lidar. So Sprout can map the room, find the light and dodge whatever's in the way. candidates.caption: Esto es lo que ve un agrónomo en campo! 🤠 Enfermedades del jitomate 🍅 #agronomo #fitopatologia #jitomate #campo #johanserratos

media.transcript: Esto es lo que un agrónomo ve cuando visita un cultivo de jitomate. Empezando por esas manchas café aterciopeladas en el embés de la hoja, son un síntoma claro de fulvia. Se trata de un hongo muy común en jitomate de invernadero bajo condiciones de humedad relativa alta. Este es el daño provocado por la araña roja. Puedes ver un punteado amarillo fino dándole una apariencia de bronceado, acompañado de telarañas finas, lo que indica una población alta, lo que conlleva una pérdida de vigor. Así es como se ve el tizón tardío, pero mucho ojo porque este no es un hongo, sino que es un homiceto. Presenta lesiones irregulares que inicialmente son acuosas o aceitosas, inician de un verde grisáceo hasta terminar de un café oscuro. Y en condiciones de alta humedad aparece un crecimiento blanquecino principalmente en el embés de la hoja. Y este es el tizón temprano provocado por alternaria, que sí, es un hongo. Y algo muy característico son esos anillos concéntricos que dan la forma de un tiro al blanco, acompañados de un halo amarillento alrededor de la lesión. Normalmente encuentras este síntoma en las hojas más viejas de la planta. Eso fue lo que encontré en este cultivo de jitomate. Coméntame si es que tú ya conocías estas enfermedades. Y pues nada, saludos.
